content:
Apple has shared more details about its Apple Music AI labeling requirements, which were first announced back in March. Here's what to expect.

AI-generated content will be clearly labeled on Apple Music

Apple earlier this year announced that Apple Music will require AI transparency disclosures for new cover art, tracks, songs, and music videos uploaded to the platform.

Now, Apple has shared more details about how this system will work.

In an email to creators today, Apple said: "Later this year, we will also make these disclosures visible to Apple Music listeners as a Made With AI label."

Apple also clarified when these disclosures are required. The email reads:

Apple Music added that its efforts are aimed at providing "maximum transparency" to listeners, and directed creators to its Style Guide for more information.

Apple Music's move is just the latest example of streaming platforms responding to the influx of AI-generated music, as more artists incorporate generative AI into their production processes.

Spotify has said that it will, by default, exclude AI Persona music from editorial and algorithmic recommendations; Deezer announced last year that fully AI-generated tracks will not appear in its recommendation and editorial playlists. Deezer also revealed last month that fully AI-generated music made up more than 50% of its daily uploads for the first time.

On the Apple Music side, the platform's head, Oliver Schusser, said earlier on Billboard's On the Record podcast that while more than one-third of the music uploaded to Apple Music each month is fully AI-generated, it accounts for less than 0.5% of streams on the service.
